To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the speedups of TreadMarks are within 15% to 50% of those of PVM, depending on the application; that the differences in speedup are due to extra messages caused by TreadMarks' design, and that eliminating the extra messages makes TreadMarks within 25% to 30% of PVM.

TreadMarks and Parallel Virtual Machine (a message-passing system) have very similar speedups for eight different applications, that the performance difference between the two systems is mostly due to the extra messages required to implement TreadMarks' synchronization protocol, that the extra messages due to access misses and false sharing are comparatively minor, and that the extra messages for migratory data are important but are reduced when diffs are accumulated.
TreadMarks is slower than PVM by 5% to 50% on a network of workstations, depending on the application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
quantifying the performance differences between TreadMarks (DSM) and PVM (MPI).
understanding the performance differences between PVM and the TreadMarks DSM system, and quantifying the effects of the performance impediments of the Treadmarks DSM system.
the performance of Treadmarks and PVM on networks of workstaions, and the differences between them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, with the exception of a few cases, the performance of Treadmarks is within 25% (and often much less) of PVM.
TreadMarks performs within a factor of 2 of PVM.
TreadMarks and the current implementation of PVM are comparable in performance for most parallel applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TreadMarks is an attractive parallel programming environment for a wide variety of applications.
, in most cases, the performance difference between PVM and the optimized TreadMarks is within 15%.
the performance of PVM and TreadsMarks are comparable for the applications studied here.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance difference between TreadMarks (and other software DSM systems) and PVM is not as great as many people believe.
, for many parallel programs, the performance difference between PVM and a distributed shared-memory system is not large.
the performance of DSM systems is not significantly lower than that of message-passing systems.
